purpose: Screen two additional San Agustin Table 1 labels against current taxonomic authority and Philippine voucher or market-provenance context.

method.scope: Focused review of Exyrias puntang and Fibramia lateralis, two printed labels in Table 1 of the 2025 San Agustin article.
method.distinction: A current broad range, a voucher from another Philippine locality, and market-sourced fish records are contextual evidence only. None identifies the 2022 San Agustin survey specimens or assigns them to a named waterbody or reach.
method.evidenceLimit: The survey article provides no voucher accession crosswalk, diagnostic images, meristic data, sequence, station coordinates, or individual reach-to-specimen link. The Fibramia market records do not independently establish capture location; the Smithsonian entry preserves a vendor-reported origin.
method.sourceReuse: Only concise attributed findings and direct source links are retained. No specimen image, market dataset, occurrence export, taxonomic table, sequence, coordinate, or transformed app row was copied. Public-app reuse approval was not assessed or granted.

findings.nameCrosswalk: The existing strict GBIF Backbone crosswalk returned an exact accepted species-rank name match (usage key 2375825; confidence 99). This is a name match only and does not identify the San Agustin specimen.
findings.currentAuthority: Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes online version updated 14 April 2026 treats Exyrias puntang as valid and summarizes an Indo-West Pacific range from Kerala and Sri Lanka east to Vanuatu and New Caledonia, north to Taiwan and the Ryukyu Islands; listed habitats are brackish and marine. The summarized range does not explicitly enumerate the Philippines.
findings.philippineContext: The California Academy of Sciences collection catalog lists voucher CAS-ICH 51479, collected 26 October 1958 at Barrio Banago, 1 km east of Siaton, Negros Oriental, from a mangrove swamp, identified as Exyrias puntang. This is a separate Philippine museum voucher and not a San Agustin fish or a present-day occurrence.
findings.disposition: The current accepted-name treatment and separate Negros Oriental voucher support Philippine context; no new range-authority discrepancy or voucher-priority mismatch is added. Retain the San Agustin label as regionally plausible but locally unresolved pending the RSU voucher/accession crosswalk and diagnostic comparison.
findings.priority: routine; request the RSU voucher/accession crosswalk and compare diagnostic characters before assigning this label to a San Agustin site or reach

findings.nameCrosswalk: The existing strict GBIF Backbone crosswalk returned an exact accepted species-rank name match (usage key 8203848; confidence 99). WoRMS AphiaID 1043449 also currently returns Fibramia lateralis with accepted status. Neither name result identifies the San Agustin specimen.
findings.currentAuthority: The 2017 Panay fish guide lists Fibramia lateralis (Valenciennes, 1832), gives an Indo-West Pacific distribution from eastern Africa to Japan and Samoa, and describes coastal-reef habitat. The entry shows voucher KAUM-I. 57198. The guide's project introduction says researchers surveyed fish markets and adjacent landing sites on Panay's south coast from 2012 to 2016 and collected or purchased about 3,000 specimens; its species entry does not provide this voucher's individual capture locality.
findings.philippineContext: The Smithsonian NMNH catalog lists USNM 435612 (field number VIS-265), identified as Fibramia lateralis and collected on 3 February 2015 at Mabini market, Bohol. The record says the vendor claimed the fish came from Mabini, Cogtong Bay. This is market-voucher context with a vendor-reported origin, not a directly verified capture coordinate. The Panay guide likewise supplies regional market-survey context, not an individual capture site.
findings.disposition: The accepted name and Philippine market-voucher context make the label nationally plausible, but neither market record independently establishes the exact capture site or identifies the San Agustin fish. No new range-authority discrepancy or voucher-priority mismatch is added. Keep the source label locally unresolved and do not turn market location or vendor testimony into a San Agustin occurrence.
findings.priority: routine; request the RSU voucher/accession crosswalk and retain collection origin and station mapping as unresolved

nextAction: Continue the current-authority and range screen for the remaining 13 of 39 Table 1 labels. Keep six voucher-priority mismatch labels in the verification queue and retain four separate range-authority discrepancies: Tridentiger trigonocephalus, Hypseleotris cyprinoides, Eleotris mauritiana, and Awaous guamensis. Then seek the RSU voucher/accession crosswalk and resolve the paper's station/locality conflicts before considering occurrence rows.

sources.supports: The original 2025 San Agustin article, its Table 1 labels, survey scope, and limitations.
